label: judge: shell-me
result:
I wrote the upgrades spec at /Users/workingmyassof/satbank/spec/v2-upgrades/shell-me.md and committed it on master as 59caa25; the repo has no remote, so nothing was pushed. It opens with a 40-row scorecard covering everything TopTierPrep has in this area: sidebar, nav, the upgrade card, account menu, floating button, sign-in, reports, profile cards, the subscription pages, classes and the phone layout. The spec as written only matched them on about 22 rows and fell short on 3 (sign-in on a new device, avatar, the log-a-mistake flow). Each of those rows now names an upgrade that makes it clearly better. There are 28 accepted upgrades, merged from the three designers. Each gives the screens and components, controls and states, data and endpoints, who builds it, how it ties into the rest of the site, and checks a verifier can run. The main ones:

- **Up next**: one queue shown on every page and reached with G N. It chains after every session and has a 5/15/30-minute option.
- **Points on the table**: each skill priced in scaled points using the same curve the score uses, and the target shown as questions right out of 44.
- **Bring your misses**: a College Board question ID, pasted text or a whole Bluebook test becomes named mistakes with fresh practice questions. 911 of the 1,030 official items map to a template we serve, and 92% of their wrong options resolve to a named reason; I measured both on the current bank.
- **Instant answer-key checks**: a separate solver re-checks the key in about a second, and one confirmed fix corrects every affected student.
- **Habits**, grouped across skills, with a drill built from the student's own mistakes.
- **Pace**, **measured-or-rough skills**, a **readiness atlas** weighted by how often each question type appears, and a **forward-looking score trend**.
- **Passkeys**, **the phone approves a shared computer**, and **per-device sign-out** with a shared-computer mode and switching between students on one device.
- **Modes that follow the exam date**, **earned spare days** for the streak, **registration deadlines**, and **reminders that say what is due**.

The document then lists 45 exact spec overrides, each quoting the current §3.1 text and giving its replacement. A separate table lists the changes needed outside §3.1: in the resolutions (R4, R9, R11, R13, R16–R18, R25) and in the schema, drill body, keyboard map and contracts. The integration task would apply those. The spare-day rule changes the one streak function (R13), and the modes change how preferences are stored (R11), so both need sign-off before the owners build them. Finally, 19 rejected ideas get one line each: offline pack, confidence tagging on every question, live class on a projector, printable class packs, a PIN on shared devices, a printed recovery card, a range switch, a bare N key, and others.
